status: Proposed bounded knowledge component; no diagnosis, treatment certification or default-branch acceptance

reuseDecision.mt_EWiY8-opdd: Asking whether a food is safe for a named person and keeping it hygienic does not require identifying common triggers, reaction categories or allergy versus intolerance.
reuseDecision.mt_q3vRl4dddK: Knowing everyday rules and when to seek a trusted adult supplies the response component, not food-specific knowledge.
reuseDecision.mt_QhLAeAlHI0: Food-group and nutrient classification can be correct without knowing that a nutritious food can cause an individual allergic reaction.
reuseDecision.mt_4JpMXUIxeD: Barrier, germ and vaccine knowledge neither requires food-allergy triggers/reactions nor distinguishes a non-allergic intolerance; its full older immune claim is not an intrinsic prerequisite.
reuseDecision.mt_Ruk2-lyGPZ: Organ order and normal digestive functions do not establish a food intolerance or immune-mediated allergy distinction.
reuseDecision.mt_CCJpSSS3l8: Nutrient comparisons and front-of-pack ratings do not determine individual allergen safety or clinical cause.

independentWitness.oldClaimsWithoutNew: A learner safely follows supplied allergy restrictions, explains food groups and germs, traces digestion and compares nutrition panels, but believes only peanuts can trigger allergy and that any stomach ache proves an allergy. All closest-card evidence may pass while the proposed trigger/reaction model fails.
independentWitness.newWithoutBroaderOld: A learner explains illustrated milk-allergy/lactose-intolerance and egg/fish cases, knows adult help is needed for suspected reactions, but cannot name the full digestive route, explain vaccine mechanisms or compare per-100 g nutrition panels. Those older whole claims are not hard gates.
independentWitness.positive: From a set including milk, egg, fish, peanuts and ordinary non-food hazards, select varied possible food triggers; connect provided known cases to possible skin/breathing/digestive reactions; contrast the two supplied milk conditions without diagnosing an unseen case.
independentWitness.nearMiss: Only peanuts can cause allergy; healthy foods cannot; all stomach pain is allergy; trying a small amount proves safety; or naming an allergen without any possible reaction explanation.
independentWitness.transfer: Change from a milk example to a known egg-allergy picture case, and then to an unexplained possible reaction: retain uncertainty, seek adult help and use supplied care instructions rather than infer diagnosis.

guideStatus: Original untested low-confidence teaching design; checked current primary bodies support content, not efficacy.

programmeCheckpoint.meaning: A new component does not by itself account for the complete source-family tasks.
